I worked through film-crew in single-shot mode first, then had banana-pro-director-2.0 write the prompt (Mode 3B, an environment plate with no people). This folder has no `NOTES.md` and isn't a git repo, so I couldn't pull or read session notes. I changed no files, so nothing needed committing. `memory/project-memory.md` has no saved facts about a mining location, so I used the following assumptions.

**Assumptions:**
- **Model:** Banana Pro on Higgsfield, 16:9, 4K.
- **Location:** a fictional highland copper mine in the Syunik region. There are no real company names, logos or flag. A flag means printed text and a symbol the model may get wrong, so you can add one later in compositing.
- **Compositing rules:** flat, neutral exposure with no grain, vignette, bloom or color grade.
- **Space for actors:** the floor near the camera and the left side of the table are kept clear, and the chairs are pushed in.

**Crew plan, in short:**
- **Director:** an empty room just before a hard meeting. The mine fills the window behind the table, so it reads as the real subject: tidy company order against damaged land.
- **Set design:**
  - A 2026 office in a mid-range regional company: light oak table, 10 black mesh chairs, water and glasses, closed notepads, a conference speakerphone.
  - A wall display that is switched off, a framed geological map with no readable text, and a hard hat and hi-vis vest on a hook.
  - A tray of drill-core samples on the sideboard.
- **Camera and light:**
  - A straight lens of about 24–28 mm at 1.3 m height, looking from the short end of the room straight down the table to the window, with everything in focus.
  - The light is soft overcast daylight from the back window, falling a little more from the right of the frame. Room lights are off.
  - The window is about 1 stop brighter than the room, so both the room and the mine stay clear.
- **For the actor shoot:** use a large soft source behind and to the right of the actors, plus a low, cool, neutral fill from the camera side. Color temperature about 6000–6500K.

**Checks:** there are no people, faces or likenesses, and no real brands or readable text. The light direction is stated and the space for actors is clear. Using a real mine's look or name in a commercial job would need your approval.

## FINAL

**Mode 3B — environment plate for compositing · Banana Pro (Higgsfield)**

**Settings:** Model: Banana Pro (Nano Banana Pro) · Aspect ratio: 16:9 · Resolution: 4K (2K for test runs) · Batch: 2–4 · References: none (if you later attach a location photo of the mine, upload it as reference 1 and it will set the view outside the window).

```
A clean, neutral photographic environment plate of an empty corporate meeting room inside the head office of a copper mining company in the high mountains of southern Armenia, present day, the camera standing at the short end of the room at a height of about 1.3 metres, looking straight down the length of a long conference table toward a wide floor-to-ceiling window on the far wall, a calm one-point perspective with the table's vanishing line leading the eye to the mine outside, the room quiet and orderly in the minutes before a difficult meeting, no one present.

The room is a modern, mid-range regional office: a long light-oak veneer conference table with a matte finish, ten black mesh office chairs pushed neatly in along both sides, a few plain glass water bottles and upturned drinking glasses on a tray at the centre, closed plain notepads with pens squared in front of several seats, a small dark conference speakerphone in the middle of the table. A large wall-mounted display hangs dark and switched off on the right-hand wall; beside it a framed geological map in muted ochres and greens, its fine lines too small to read. Along the left wall a low grey sideboard holds a shallow wooden tray of grey-green drill-core samples, and near the window a white hard hat and a folded high-visibility vest hang on a wall hook. Pale grey walls, a dark charcoal carpet tile floor, recessed ceiling light panels switched off. The open floor in the foreground and the walkway along the left side of the table stay clear and uncluttered, leaving room for figures to be added later.

Through the window the land is the true subject: a vast terraced open-pit copper mine cut into the mountainside, its stepped benches descending in bands of rust, burnt ochre, ash grey and oxidised grey-green rock, a dusty haul road switching back down the pit walls with a few small yellow haul trucks far below, pale tailings terraces at the edge, and beyond them bare, treeless highland ridges fading into low, heavy grey cloud. The distant ridges soften slightly in the damp mountain air, while the pit itself stays crisp and fully detailed.

The only light is soft, flat overcast daylight from the large window on the far wall, falling into the room slightly more from frame-right, giving a gentle, low-contrast wash across the tabletop, soft directionless shadows under the chairs, and a faint cool sheen on the matte table surface. The exposure is balanced so the room interior and the landscape outside are both fully readable, the window only about one stop brighter than the room, with no clipped highlights in the clouds and open, detailed shadows indoors.

Shot as a neutral reference plate on a real full-frame cinema camera with a clean, sharp spherical wide lens around 24 to 28 millimetres, straight vertical lines, deep focus from the foreground chairs to the far mountains, natural true-to-life colour with neutral white balance, accurate copper and ochre tones in the rock, even flat exposure, crisp but natural detail. Real photographic frame of a real office and a real mountain mine under a real overcast sky — no CGI, no rendered look, no plastic surfaces, no AI smoothness, no film grain, no vignette, no bloom or halation, no lens flare, no colour grade, no people, no readable text, no logos.
```
